set.text: Our soccer team played the Blue Hawks on Sunday. In the morning, it started to rain. We played anyway. The ball was hard to control on the wet grass. At the end, the Blue Hawks won by one goal. Coach Park said, 'You all played hard. Keep trying!' We still had fun.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “trying” mean?
options: working hard to do something well
tasting something to see if you like it
qs.why: The coach wants the players to keep working hard to play well. Here it does not mean tasting food, and it is the opposite of giving up.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “control” mean?
options: to make it go where you want
to find it after losing it
qs.why: On wet grass the ball was hard to make go where the players wanted.

qs.q: Did the writer's team win the game?
options: No, they lost by one goal, but they still had fun
Yes, they won by one goal
No, the game was stopped by the rain
Yes, and the coach said they were the best
No, and they were very sad
No one won; the score was the same
qs.why: The Blue Hawks won by one goal, so the writer's team lost. But the writer says 'We still had fun.'

why: Soccer is scored in goals, not points: 'won by one point' was wrong for soccer. Changed to 'one goal' and swapped v-point for v-try (coach now says 'Keep trying!') with a new word question.

set.text: Today the Okafor family is moving to a new house. Dad carries big boxes to the truck. Mom puts her guitar in its case so it will not break. Little Ada holds her cat. She feels a bit sad to leave her old room. But her new room has a big window that looks out on a park.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “case” mean?
options: a box or cover that keeps things safe
qs.why: Mom puts her guitar in its case so it will not break, so the case keeps it safe.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “bit” mean?
qs.why: Ada is a little sad, but the next sentence says her new room is nice.

options: Her new room is very small
She cannot go to the park
She has to leave her old room
She does not like the truck
qs.why: The passage says she feels sad to leave her old room. Her new room has a big window, so it is not small.

why: 'Puts her best cups in a soft case' is unnatural English (cups go in a box); changed to a guitar in its case, the natural use of the card meaning.

set.text: The Patel family was driving to the beach. Suddenly, the car made a strange noise and stopped. Dad got out and looked at the car. 'I don't know what is wrong,' he said. Mom called a man who fixes cars. He came in his truck one hour later. He fixed the problem fast. His service cost fifty dollars. Soon they were on the road again.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “service” mean?
options: a set of plates for dinner
the work the man did for them
qs.why: The man fixed the car, and that work cost fifty dollars. It was not free.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “wrong” mean?
options: not the way it should be
qs.why: The car stopped, so something in it was not the way it should be.
Dad did not know what was wrong. Mom called a man who fixes cars, and he fixed the problem.

why: 'Called a service that fixes cars' uses service as 'a business', and the keyed option said 'a business', not the card meaning (work done for others). Rewrote so 'His service cost fifty dollars' = the work he did; updated both affected questions.

set.text: The city government wants to make a new law. Dogs in the park must walk next to their owners. This rule matters a lot to dog owners. Some like the idea, and some do not. So next Tuesday there will be a meeting at City Hall. Anyone can come and talk about it. Officer Grant from the police will answer questions. The doors will be open at six o'clock.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “matters” mean?
options: is a thing you can touch
qs.why: The rule is important to dog owners because it changes how they walk their dogs.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “open” mean?
options: not closed, so people can go in
qs.why: At six o'clock the doors will not be closed, so people can go in to the meeting. 'Locked' is the opposite.

qs.q: Why will there be a meeting?
options: To pick a new police officer
To say the law is already done
So people can talk about the new dog law
qs.why: Some people like the idea and some do not, so there is a meeting where anyone can talk about it.

why: 'Open to all' (available to everyone) is a different sense from the card (not closed, so things can go in or out). Rewrote to 'The doors will be open at six o'clock' and rebuilt the open question.

set.text: Grandpa Femi has a box of photos. One rainy afternoon, he looks at them with his granddaughter, Zara. 'This is me when I was young,' he says. 'And this girl is your grandma. We met at a birthday party.' He smiles. 'I remember the music and the cake. It was a special day.' Zara asks him to tell her more.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “party” mean?
options: a group that wants to run the government
a time when people meet to eat and have fun
qs.why: A birthday party has music and cake, so it is a time for fun. It is not a political party here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “remember” mean?
options: still has it in his mind; does not forget
qs.why: Many years later, Grandpa still has the music and the cake in his mind. He did not forget them.
Grandpa says, 'We met at a birthday party.' The rainy afternoon is when he shows Zara the photos.

why: The text uses present 'I remember', but the options were past tense ('forgot', 'did not forget'); put all options in matching present form.

set.text: Last year, Nadia's family moved to a new country. At first, school was hard for her. She did not speak any English, and she was sure she would never make friends. But a girl named Lily sat with her at lunch, and she did not miss a single day. Now Nadia speaks English well, and Lily is her best friend.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “hard” mean?
qs.why: School was not easy because Nadia did not speak English. “Not soft” is another meaning of hard.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “never” mean?
qs.why: Nadia thought there would be no time at all when she would make friends.

options: She sat with her at lunch every day
qs.why: Lily sat with Nadia at lunch and did not miss a single day.

why: 'Lily did not miss a single day' could mean Lily never missed school, so the keyed idea answer ('sat with her at lunch every day') was not clearly supported. Joined the sentences so it ties to lunch.
